chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Kindi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Jibraeel (peace be upon him) said to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): 'Beware of disputing with the men.'
ai.seo_question: What does the term 'mulahatah' mean in the context of this hadith from Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, the Angel Jibraeel (AS) conveys divine advice to the Prophet (SAWW) to avoid 'mulahatah', a term often interpreted by Shia scholars as engaging in idle quarreling or superficial disputes with people. This narration underscores the spiritual discipline of preserving inner peace and social harmony by refraining from unnecessary verbal conflict, a key aspect of Prophetic character (Sunnah).

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al Hassan Bin Al Husayn Al Kindy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> said to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>: ‘Beware of disputing the men’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-Hassan ibn al-Husayn al-Kindy from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“Jibril (Gabriel) said to the Holy Prophet, ‘Beware of engaging in disputes against men.’”
